newsitem.title: USA: NATIONAL CARLOT BEEF TRADE WEEKLY REVIEW - USDA.
newsitem.headline: NATIONAL CARLOT BEEF TRADE WEEKLY REVIEW - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was sharply lower on moderate demand and heavy offerings, USDA said. Improved retail demand was noted for both immediate and future needs after two weeks of rather light demand.

Chuck and round cuts traded lower throughout the week as inventories were rather large and burdensome. Rib and loin cuts also traded lower throughout the week with the most downward pressure on the loin cuts as these cuts lost all of last week's big increases.
Closely trimmed items also traded sharply lower on fairly good demand as these cuts continue to be good values.

Beef trimmings traded lower on light to moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings. Good frozen interest was noted late in the trading period. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded lower early in the week, but rebounded as the week progressed, and ended at steady levels compared to last week.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 4.00 to 9.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 3.00 to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 4.00 to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 6.00 to 9.00 lower; Closely trimmed items 4.00 to 5.00 lower; Beef trimmings 2.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 4.21 at 104.44; 700/850 Dn 4.74 at 104.13; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 5.21 at 96.61; 700/850 Dn 5.38 at 96.06.
COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Demand for boneless beef was light as fast food business shifted to other protein promotions.

The boneless beef market was sharply lower this week as demand was light causing offerings to mound. However, as prices fell thoughout the week product started to clear the market. The cow carcass market traded lower on light to moderate demand and offerings.

The cow cuts moved lower on light demand and moderate to heavy offerings. The 100% lean supermill and flats and eyes traded lower on light to moderate demand and heavy offerings. Utility 1.00 lower; Cutter carcasses not established; 90% boneless beef 6.00-7.00 lower in the Midwest, Texas 8.00-8.50 lower; 85% 5.00-6.00 lower; 75% 5.00 lower; 65% not established. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, August 8, 1997 was estimated at 78.75 per cwt., down 4.15 from a week ago Friday.
